messages.author: 25e13e522040f0b9
messages.subject: Plot of all QTL locations
parts:
Hi Karl,

I'm trying to make a figure like Fig. 1 in this paper and attached here (i.e. plot the peak of multiple QTLs and their Bayes intervals for multiple traits on a chromosome grid like the one used for plotting scanone results). Do you have a suggestion for how to do this? Even a few pointers would be helpful.

Thank you

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Plot of all QTL locations
parts:
I tend to use a segments() for this sort of thing.

Call plot() with type="n" and xlim, ylim giving the right x- and y-axis limits
Call abline() with v = chromosome boundaries
Loop through the chromosomes:
Call segments for all of the horizontal intervals
Call segments again for the vertical ticks

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Plot of all QTL locations
parts:
Andres, Here is another option, though Karl's works well and I use that too.
If you have a data.frame of statistics (position, lg, ci bounds, etc), you can use a custom function I wrote to produce graphs that look like this (attached).
There is a basic description of how to use it here: https://johntlovell.files.wordpress.com/2014/10/stepwisesummary.pdf.  You can also combine lodprofile plots in this function.
If you need help, send me an email.
John

John Lovell
Postdoc, University of Texas at Austin.
